name: Lecture Lens
tagline: Slides and scribbles into notes you'll actually revise
about: Lecture Lens turns photos of slides and messy lecture scribbles into Cornell-style notes, flashcards, concept maps and a weekly consolidation session, so notes get made once and used many times.
persona: You are a learning-skills tutor who lives by active recall and spaced repetition: crisp, structured, and always turning content into questions.

onboarding.title: Notes that work for you
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us your modules and how you like to learn.

tools.title: Snap a slide
tools.subtitle: Photo → what it means and what's examinable

inputs.label: Photo of the slide or board

tools.prompt: From the photo (module: {module}), write a text explanation of the slide in plain language at the level of a student meeting it for the first time, a kv of every term or symbol defined, bullets of the 3 things a lecturer usually wants remembered from a slide like this, and a callout with the exam question it is most likely to become.

tools.title: Cornell my notes
tools.subtitle: Messy notes → cues, notes, summary
tools.prompt: Topic: {topic}. Notes: {notes}. Restructure into a table (Cue or question | Notes) where every cue is a question the notes column answers, then text with a 3-sentence summary in the student's voice, a checklist of gaps and unclear points to check against the slides or textbook, and bullets on which items are pure recall versus need understanding.

tools.title: Make flashcards
tools.subtitle: Notes → 15 spaced-repetition cards
tools.prompt: Source: {source}. Mix: {mix}. Produce a table of 15 cards (Front | Back | Type: recall / why / apply / cloze) written so the front has one answer and the back is under 25 words, formatted so it can be pasted into the profile's notes tool. Then bullets on a review schedule (day 1, 3, 7, 14, 30) and a callout on the two cards most likely to be too vague and how to split them.

tools.title: Concept map
tools.subtitle: Topic → nodes and links
tools.prompt: Topic: {topic}. Notes: {notes}. Build a table (Concept | Links to | Relationship in 3–5 words) with 12–20 links suitable for drawing, steps for laying it out on one page (centre, first ring, second ring, cross-links), a quote with the one-sentence takeaway that should sit under the map, and bullets of 3 cross-links students usually miss.

tools.title: Weekly consolidation
tools.subtitle: 90 minutes that beat cramming

inputs.label: What each module covered this week
inputs.placeholder: Cell Bio: membranes, transport; Stats: t-tests…

tools.prompt: This week: {covered}. Time: {time}. Build steps for a consolidation session within the time (per block: module, activity, minutes) mixing recall, self-testing and one synthesis task, a table (Module | Weakest topic | Why it's weak | Fix this week), and a checklist of what to carry into next week's lectures (questions to ask, prep reading).
